caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:000678
attempts.paper_title: Hulsey, D., Zumwalt, K., Mazzucato, L., McCormick, D. A., & Jaramillo, S. (2024). Decision-making dynamics are predicted by arousal and uninstructed movements. Cell Reports, 43(1), 113709.
attempts.entry_title: Arousal, uninstructed movements and decision-making states in mice (Hulsey et al. 2024)
attempts.summary: Most main findings held up in this data, one did not, and one could not be tested. Mice moved between optimal, disengaged and sub-optimal states, the optimal state was the longest lasting, and its probability followed an inverted U of pupil diameter. Variability was lower in the optimal state, and arousal measures classified states above chance. The claim that a movement index predicts state better than pupil did not reproduce (68.6% against 71.5%), and the variants that favour it keep pupil information. Training duration could not be tested because sessions before stage 5 are missing, and some dwell time values only partly matched.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Hulsey, Zumwalt, Mazzucato, McCormick and Jaramillo (2024) on dandiset 000678, which holds the stage 5 and 6 behavioral sessions of 13 mice performing auditory or visual discrimination, with pupil diameter, face motion energy and locomotion speed. It fits the paper's GLM-HMM to each mouse's choices, labels the performance states, and relates the states to the arousal and movement measures, including the support vector machine decoding of the states.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Hulsey et al. (2024) from dandiset 000678

outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds 13 mice, 8 on the auditory and 5 on the visual task, each with at least 10 passing sessions. Of its 391 stage 5 and 6 sessions, 376 pass the STAR Methods criteria counted from the reward series and 375 counted from the hits, against 381 in the paper. The sessions failing either count are listed in the notebook; 14 fail both (13 with fewer than 100 rewards, 1 with less than 20% at one port) and 3 fail one count only. The paper's 500 stage 5 and 6 sessions and its 18 excluded mice are not in the dandiset.
deviations: The sessions of every later analysis are the 376 that pass the criteria by the reward count; the paper analysed 381, and the dandiset does not say which.

outcomes.notes: Every session in the dandiset is stage 5 or 6 (metadata training_stage), so the training sessions before stage 5 cannot be counted. They are not public elsewhere as far as the paper and the dandiset say.

Distractor trials have outcome 4 (false alarm, a lick) or 8 (correct reject). Under reading (c), 2,446 of 47,037 stage 6 distractor trials had a lick, 5.2%. Under readings (a) and (b), 7 of the 8 mice with stage 6 sessions are below 10%; BW053 is at 16.2% pooled and 15.3% over sessions. "No discriminable change in performance" is not tested; the fraction correct of responded target trials differs between stages by at most 5.4 points.

With 10 random initialisations per fold, as the paper, both readings of O1 give 3 states in five mice and 4 in eight, inside the claimed 3 to 5 as the criterion requires; no mouse has 5 states, so the largest count is 4 against the paper's 5. The MAP plateau is never larger than the MLE plateau. 38 of the 9,100 cross-validation fits stopped at 1,000 iterations.
deviations: The GLM-HMM of the paper's ssm fork is reimplemented (hulsey.py) with the same model, priors, initialisation scheme, EM updates and stopping rule; its random initial values differ from ssm's. The test log probability includes the log prior, as ssm's log_probability does.

The visual stimulus values follow loadbehavior.get_stim_vals of the paper's code (uobrainflex at ef48985), which for a file with a visual_gabor_angle column maps the difficulty codes 0, 1 and 2 to the session's distinct values of abs(angle - 45) / 45, largest first, and otherwise to 1, 0.8 and 0.6. 118 of the 141 visual-task sessions get 1, 0.6 and 0.2 and the other 23 get 1, 0.8 and 0.6. The first version of this attempt used 1, 0.8 and 0.6 for every session.
Fit on the 376 sessions that pass the inclusion criteria (see cohort-inclusion).

outcomes.notes: BW046 gets 4 states under both readings of O1; one-state accuracy 70.2%, 4-state accuracy 78.1%, computed as in fig2d-prediction-accuracy.
deviations: As for figs2-n-states and fig2d-prediction-accuracy.

outcomes.notes: All 13 mice have an optimal, a disengaged and at least one other state, and each of the 21 other states is matched to a sub-optimal template. Mice per type are bias left 6, avoid right 5, bias right 6 and avoid left 4 (Figure 2A gives 6, 4, 5 and 5; not deciding). Under M3 the other states are matched only to the four sub-optimal templates, so that part of the criterion cannot fail; the distances to all six templates, printed for BW061 and BW048, put each of their states nearest the template of its label. In BW059 one state has no trial with a posterior of at least 0.8 in the sessions where the optimal state occurs, so its psychometric is all missing; Figure2.py's nansum would score it 0 against every template and mislabel the mouse's optimal state. That state (432 trials over all sessions) is typed on all sessions, as avoid right. The question is asked of the paper's authors (findings).
deviations: Assumption. A state with no discrete-state trial in the sessions where the optimal state occurs is typed on all of the mouse's sessions; Figure2.py has no rule for it (it would score the state as equal to every template). Affects one state of BW059.
As for figs2-n-states.

outcomes.notes: On sessions in which the optimal state occurs, the optimal state holds 50.5% +/- 3.3% of trials, disengaged 12.7%, sub-optimal 23.7% and indeterminate 13.1% +/- 1.6%, within the expected 13.1 +/- 1.6. The optimal share is larger than each other share in 13 of 13 mice (Wilcoxon signed-rank p = 0.00024 for each).
deviations: As for figs2-n-states.

outcomes.notes: Optimal epochs are longer than disengaged and sub-optimal epochs in 13 of 13 mice under every reading (p = 0.00024). The median indeterminate dwell is 3.31 +/- 0.35 trials, within 3.4 +/- 0.3. The 37 is not matched under any reading. Under reading (a) the optimal dwell is 43.8 trials with the code's dwell (y) and 42.8 as run length (x), above 40.7; the disengaged dwell is 14.0 (13.8), within 15 +/- 1.5, and the sub-optimal 19.1 (18.1), above it. Readings (b) and (c) give optimal dwells of 73.2 to 74.1 and 49.3 to 50.3. The measured values are the indeterminate dwell and the optimal and disengaged dwells under (a) and (y).
deviations: flex_hmm.get_dwell_times adds a last epoch of dwell 0 when a session's last trial differs from the one before it, which also adds a zero indeterminate dwell. The code's output is used, as the claims file reads it; without the 3 such epochs the indeterminate dwell and the medians are unchanged (shown in the notebook).
As for figs2-n-states.

outcomes.notes: Best model 76.2% +/- 1.6%, one state 65.1% +/- 2.2%, gain 11.0 +/- 1.3 points under reading (a) (17.8% +/- 2.5% relative under (b), outside). Better in 13 of 13 mice, Wilcoxon signed-rank p = 0.00024 (rank-sum p = 0.00025).
deviations: The paper's code computes the filtered posterior of the preceding test trials by re-running expected_states on each prefix; here one forward pass gives the same filtered probabilities.
As for figs2-n-states.

outcomes.notes: Reading (i) holds in 13 of 13 mice and reading (ii) in 13 of 13, so "nearly all" holds under (a) and (b). Polynomial degrees 2 to 6 were selected by the elbow rule.
deviations: As Figure3.py, a state absent from a bin with more than 5 trials leaves that bin missing, so a bin with no optimal trial is not a zero; this follows the code.
As for figs2-n-states.

outcomes.notes: Median optimal pupil 0.649 of the session maximum for the 8 auditory mice and 0.739 for the 5 visual mice; Wilcoxon rank-sum p = 0.013 (exact Mann-Whitney p = 0.011; paper 0.008).

On all trials, over 23 bins with at least 7 mice, the second-order fit to mean P(optimal) has a negative quadratic term (vertex -0.9% from the optimal pupil) and to P(disengaged) a positive one (vertex -1.6%). On stationary trials under reading (b), absolute speed below 0.02 m/s (32,495 trials, 21 bins), both hold (vertices -3.3 and -6.1). Counting the 214 trials at or below -0.02 m/s as stationary, as the first version did, changes the vertices by at most 0.1. Reading (a), speed exactly 0, leaves 1,821 trials and no bin with 7 mice, so it cannot be tested. Exact zeros depend on rounding in the filter (9,869 more trials have a speed below 1e-9 m/s that is not exactly 0), and a run on another machine counted 1,879.
deviations: Stationary under reading (b) is taken as absolute speed below 0.02 m/s, so that backward movement is not counted as stationary.

outcomes.notes: Pupil r2 0.690 +/- 0.039 (within 0.72 +/- 0.03). Face 0.428 +/- 0.092 with plotting bins (a), within, and 0.409 with 50 bins (b), just outside. Locomotion 0.567 (a), outside (0.570 in a run on another machine), and 0.413 (b), within. No bin reading puts all three in tolerance. Both are lower than pupil on average (by 0.12 to 0.28), but by Wilcoxon only locomotion under (b) is lower at p < 0.05 (p = 0.011); face p = 0.11 and 0.057, locomotion (a) p = 0.41. The criterion's r2 comes from one shuffled split per mouse, as 4_optimal_pupils.py; the mean over 10 splits gives pupil 0.682 +/- 0.043 (BW051 from 0.001 to 0.562 over the splits) and the same test results (face p = 0.15 and 0.068, locomotion p = 0.34 and 0.013). The measured values are pupil, face (a) and locomotion (a).
deviations: As for figs2-n-states.

outcomes.notes: The mean P(optimal) over the 0.25 movement-index bins with at least 7 mice has a negative quadratic term with its vertex at 0.28, inside -4.25 to 3.75. The r2 is 0.574 +/- 0.057 under (a), within 0.63 +/- 0.06 and close to its lower bound, and 0.533 under (b), outside. It does not differ from pupil's (difference -0.12, p = 0.22 under (a); p = 0.17 under (b)). Over 10 shuffled splits per mouse the r2 is 0.573 (a) and 0.522 (b).
deviations: As for figs2-n-states.

outcomes.notes: The mean P(disengaged) over 34 movement-index bins with at least 7 mice has a positive quadratic term (0.0225) with its vertex at 0.08, inside -4.25 to 4.0.

The two correlations agree to better than 0.0001 in every mouse (as they must by construction), with r from 0.674 to 0.855; reading (b), above 0.5, holds, and reading (a), above 0.7, fails in BW071 (0.674).

Under reading (a) of O3 the absolute distance is 8.8% +/- 1.0% in the optimal state, 16.0% in the disengaged and 11.8% in the sub-optimal states, lower in the optimal state than in the disengaged (13 of 13, p = 0.00024) and sub-optimal states (13 of 13, p = 0.00024); reading (b) gives 8.8, 15.8 and 11.5 (p = 0.00024 and 0.0012). The order and the tests hold; all three values are larger than the paper's 7, 12.6 and 9.
deviations: Rests on the optimal pupils of fig3c-inverted-u-pupil, from this attempt's state fits.

outcomes.notes: Reading (a) of O3 gives 0.482, 0.441 and 0.448 a.u., all within tolerance; optimal is the largest, above sub-optimal with p = 0.017 and above disengaged with p = 0.19 (paper 0.06). Reading (b) gives 0.485, 0.435 and 0.453 (p = 0.048 and 0.08).

Optimal 0.136, disengaged 0.137, sub-optimal 0.136 m/s under reading (a), differences of at most 0.002 m/s, p = 0.84 and 0.89; reading (b) 0.137, 0.132 and 0.139 m/s, p = 0.68 and 0.95. Speeds are read as m/s although the file labels them cm/s (findings).

All six differences have the stated sign. Pupil, optimal against disengaged p = 0.00024 and against sub-optimal p = 0.0012; face p = 0.0024 and 0.017; locomotion p = 0.0012 and 0.057. Five of six tests pass.

All six changes have the stated sign on average over mice (entry, pupil 0.0319 to 0.0283, face 0.0750 to 0.0680, locomotion 0.0620 to 0.0545; exit, 0.0301 to 0.0346, 0.0713 to 0.0780, 0.0553 to 0.0640). Of the four comparisons the figure marks, pupil exit (p = 0.0012), locomotion entry (p = 0.04) and locomotion exit (p = 0.0012) pass, face entry (p = 0.11) does not. 9 to 85 entries and 18 to 125 exits per mouse.

Mean r 0.077 (optimal), 0.439 (disengaged), 0.267 (sub-optimal); optimal lower than disengaged in 13 of 13 (p = 0.00024) and than sub-optimal in 12 of 13 (p = 0.00049). Disengaged is higher than sub-optimal (p = 0.0081), as the figure marks.

Pupil with face, optimal lower than disengaged (p = 0.0024) and sub-optimal (p = 0.00049). Pupil with locomotion, lower than disengaged (p = 0.0017), not significantly lower than sub-optimal (p = 0.068). The face with locomotion correlation is also lower in the optimal state (p = 0.00049 and 0.01).

Median r with the preceding ITI, pupil -0.044, locomotion -0.007, face -0.044, none different from zero (p = 0.13, 0.89, 0.27), so the ITI part holds under readings (a) and (b). The Kruskal-Wallis test of the per-mouse median evoked pupil response over the four groups gives H = 4.38, p = 0.22 (three discrete states, p = 0.15); group means -1.19, 1.57, 0.2 and -0.51% of the maximum.
deviations: The pupil at onset is the filtered value at the stimulus sample; FigureS1.py takes it from the trial's pupil trace, 1 ms later. A standard choice that cannot change the result.

outcomes.notes: Optimal fits, pupil squared, locomotion squared, pupil SD and locomotion SD weights negative (medians -1.11, -1.10, -0.26, -0.33; Wilcoxon against zero p = 0.00024, 0.0012, 0.0081, 0.027). Disengaged fits, the same weights positive (0.56, 0.64, 0.19, 0.20; p = 0.00049, 0.00024, 0.033, 0.0081). Face squared and face SD weights do not differ from zero (p 0.19 to 0.84). Reading (a) holds, and so does (b).

Pupil-by-movement weight 0.41 +/- 0.10 over 21 sub-optimal fits and -0.95 +/- 0.21 over 13 optimal fits, rank-sum p = 3.8e-06; quadratic movement weight of the optimal fits -1.30. Among the sub-optimal weights only the interaction differs from zero (p below 0.001).

Eight features unshuffled (condition 13), 88.9% +/- 1.7% over 13 optimal against disengaged classifications and 78.4% +/- 1.8% over 20 optimal against sub-optimal classifications; the "All measures" condition 0 gives 88.5% and 77.7%. All 33 classifications are significant under readings (a), (b) and (c). The paper has 19 sub-optimal classifications; this attempt's fits give 21 sub-optimal states, 20 with enough trials.
deviations: 3 runs per shuffled condition and 20 null runs, in place of 1000, to fit the time limit. The unshuffled condition does not vary between runs. With 20 null runs the null SD and its 95th percentile are estimated less precisely.
Rests on this attempt's state fits (figs2-n-states).

outcomes.notes: Reading (a), accuracy, pupil 71.5%, face 66.1%, locomotion 68.1%; pupil above face in 24 of 33 (p = 0.0011) and above locomotion on average (p = 0.053; 0.051 in a run on another machine). The z-scores and reading (b) agree for face (p from 0.00029 to 0.0013); under (b) pupil is also above locomotion (p = 0.029 and 0.022).
deviations: As for fig5c-state-classification.

outcomes.notes: Main reading (movement index value and SD kept, all else shuffled) gives 68.6% against 71.5% for pupil alone, movement higher in 14 of 33 (p = 0.086); z 4.51 against 5.21 (p = 0.068). The movement index is not better than pupil. The code's conditions shown as variants give higher accuracy for the movement-index classifier, condition 5 (movement index kept with the pupil value) 75.7% (p = 1.3e-05) and condition 1 (face and locomotion shuffled) 77.9% (p = 2.3e-10), but both keep pupil information, so they compare pupil and movement together against pupil alone and do not test the claim.
deviations: As for fig5c-state-classification.

findings.statement: The running_speed series of every file is labelled cm/s, but its values (session medians around 0.07, 99th percentiles up to 0.67) are in m/s, the unit of the paper and of its code.

The dandiset holds 391 stage 5 and 6 sessions of the 13 included mice, where the paper analysed 381. The paper's inclusion criteria select 376 of them counted from the reward series and 375 counted from the hits, and nothing in the dandiset marks which sessions the paper used.

The training sessions before stage 5, the other stage 5 and 6 sessions of the 500 the paper names, and the 18 mice that did not meet the inclusion criteria are not in the dandiset, so the training duration (21 +/- 8 sessions) cannot be tested.
In 38 of the 391 sessions the post hoc pupil diameter series is present but entirely missing values (14 of BW046's 34 sessions), so those sessions have no pupil measure.
The rig names in the session metadata are spelled several ways for what appear to be the same rigs (Box 1, Box1, Boox1).

Question for the paper's authors. Figure2.py types each state by its nearest template with nansum, so a state with no trial of posterior 0.8 or more in the sessions where the optimal state occurs scores 0 against every template and displaces the optimal label. In this attempt's fits one state of BW059 is such a state; it was typed on all sessions. How were such states handled, and which 381 sessions were analysed?
